brief: Goldman's Flood frames the week around Friday's jobs print: payrolls +165k versus roughly 65k expected calmed the growth-scare narrative but pushed December hike odds above 80%, with core CPI due tomorrow (GIR forecasts +16bps MoM) and the S&P's implied move through Friday at 2.29%. Since October, GS clients have net sold $30bn of tech stocks (TMT and Communication Services), $6bn of it last week, versus $23bn sold during July's momentum drawdown; Friday 11/6 broke a seven-session tech-selling streak with a $1bn buyskew. Investors are repricing 2028 datacenter capex growth lower after the midterm election (Texas, Ohio), to well below the prior 30-40%+ y/y expectation, a level clients and Flood see as an attractive entry point. PB data show the largest weekly gross-leverage drop since Covid and the largest net-leverage drop since Liberation Day, with L/S hedge funds down 50bps and Global Systematics down 150bps last week. Flood stays constructive on 35% y/y EPS growth, improving breadth, cheap P/E and buybacks.
